title: Four guards at the gate
hookLine: four guards at one gate, and a way past all of them
carry: befriend one gatekeeper, and it brings the rest
tomorrow: a queen's husband dies. where is he now? the goddess shows her.

lines: A DEADLINE, A CROWD OF GUARDS.
cards: A big decision with a deadline can feel like a gate with a crowd of guards in front of it: the money, the people, the fear, the forms. Vasistha draws Rama a gate like that.
It leads to moksha, freedom, the thing Rama's questions have been reaching for. Four guards stand at it. Getting past all four at once looks hopeless.

teach.b: Vasistha names them: shama, a calm mind; vichara, honest inquiry into what's real; santosha, contentment with what one has; and satsanga, the company of the wise and good. Then the kind part.
Rama doesn't have to win all four.
Befriend even one, Vasistha says, and it brings you to the others. Start with the nearest.
Now look back across the week.

teach.h: ONE FRIEND BRINGS THE OTHER THREE.
teach.b: The Kama Sutra's ethics chapter drew a family tree, three aims from one teaching. It let pleasure's critics speak, and answered with barley and deer. It let dharma's critics speak, and answered with a farmer's seed.
It closed on mastery of the senses. Then a new book, and a prince who'd lost his taste for all of it, met not with a scolding but with a teacher. Then two rams in a field.
Two very different books, both circling one question: how a person holds the world.

how: Teachers in the Vedanta tradition sometimes quote the four gatekeepers to students who feel stuck, with the advice to start with whichever one is closest.

o: a sage's teaching: befriend one guard of freedom first
a list of four sins a seeker must give up for good
a story about four soldiers guarding a royal palace

games.q: your aunt asks you to come to the monthly satsang at the temple hall: bhajans, a short talk, chai after. a friend asks why it matters. by Vasistha's gate, what's the answer?
o: satsanga is one of freedom's four guards; befriend it, and it brings the others.
it doesn't; freedom comes only from sitting alone.
you have to master calm and contentment first, then you're allowed to go.
games.why: satsanga, the company of the wise and good, is one of Vasistha's four gatekeepers of moksha. befriend even one, he tells Rama, and it brings you to the rest.

practice: Count four things on your fingers, one for each guard: a moment of calm you had this week, one honest question you've been asking, one thing you have that's enough, and one person whose company makes you better.
Let each finger rest a moment before the next, and give thanks, in whatever way is yours.

wordCard.voice: The Yoga Vasistha: four gatekeepers of freedom, and befriending one brings the rest.
